AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why are diseased plants not added to compost? (1 mark)
   A. They rot too slowly to count
   B. The disease can spread to the crops later
   C. They are too heavy
   D. They make the heap too tall

2. Why does compost help the environment? (1 mark)
   A. It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   B. It kills all soil animals
   C. It uses up all the water
   D. It creates more rubbish

3. Why do we sprinkle soil or old compost between layers? (1 mark)
   A. It adds plastic
   B. It keeps birds away
   C. It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   D. It makes the heap sweeter

4. Why is meat kept out of a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. It turns into plastic
   B. It makes the compost too dry
   C. It kills the soil
   D. It attracts rats and flies and smells bad

5. Which sign shows that compost is ready? (1 mark)
   A. It is grey and hard
   B. It is wet and smells sour
   C. It is hot and full of whole peelings
   D. It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth

6. What does mulch do? (1 mark)
   A. Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   B. Adds plastic to the soil
   C. Makes the soil hot
   D. Kills the plant

7. What might happen if the water for a drip system is dirty? (1 mark)
   A. The holes may block
   B. The plants will grow faster
   C. The bucket will be lighter
   D. The water will taste better

8. Why should the end of the drip pipe be closed? (1 mark)
   A. So rainwater cannot enter
   B. So the plants do not drink
   C. So water does not run out of the end
   D. So the pipe looks nice

9. How is charcoal made? (1 mark)
   A. By mixing soil and water
   B. By boiling water
   C. By drying maize
   D. By burning wood slowly with little air

10. Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole? (1 mark)
   A. A tin of paint
   B. A knife on the pole
   C. A bare hand only
   D. A hammer or heavy stone to push it in

11. What is direct sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Buying young plants
   B. Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   C. Sowing in a nursery
   D. Watering seeds

12. What does sowing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting a crop
   B. Watering a crop
   C. Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   D. Storing seeds

13. Why are weeds removed from the seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. They take water, light and food from the crop
   B. They protect seedlings from rain
   C. They add manure
   D. They are colourful

14. Why should a container seedbed have holes at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. Extra water can drain out
   B. Insects can leave
   C. Seeds can escape
   D. To make it lighter

15. What is the main job of the trunk of a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Make flowers
   B. Absorb sunlight
   C. Collect rain
   D. Carry water and food between roots and leaves

16. What is a tree tomato? (1 mark)
   A. A cereal
   B. A vegetable that grows underground
   C. A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   D. A climbing vine

17. When should fruits be harvested? (1 mark)
   A. When they are ripe
   B. After they rot
   C. While green and hard
   D. Before flowers appear

18. Which is a way of protecting ripe fruit from birds and monkeys? (1 mark)
   A. Poison the animals
   B. Cut the tree
   C. Leave them ripe for months
   D. Cover trees with nets or use scare methods

19. Which is likely to take longest to give fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Passion fruit
   B. Pawpaw
   C. Radish
   D. Mango tree

20. Why should the soil be firmed around a newly planted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   B. To dry the roots
   C. To hide it
   D. To make the plant fall

21. What is the meat of sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Beef
   B. Bacon
   C. Pork
   D. Mutton

22. What is the meat from cattle called? (1 mark)
   A. Beef
   B. Chicken
   C. Pork
   D. Mutton

23. What is the young one of a hen called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Lamb
   C. Kid
   D. Chick

24. Which nutrient do body-building foods supply? (1 mark)
   A. Protein
   B. Salt
   C. Fibre only
   D. Water

25. What is one way to choose foods for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Pick only sweet food
   B. Pick only your favourite food
   C. Pick one or more foods from each group
   D. Pick only cheap food

26. Which of these belongs to more than one group? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Groundnuts
   C. Water
   D. Sugar

27. Which of these gives fibre? (1 mark)
   A. Sweets
   B. Sugar
   C. Soft drinks
   D. Vegetables and fruits

28. Which food is usually boiled? (1 mark)
   A. Mandazi
   B. Potatoes
   C. Bhajia
   D. Chips

29. What should you hold hot pots with? (1 mark)
   A. Bare hands
   B. A wet cloth
   C. A dry cloth or oven gloves
   D. Paper

30. About how long are eggs boiled for hard-boiled eggs? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 hours
   B. One second
   C. About 10 minutes
   D. About 10 seconds

31. How often should you brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Twice a day
   B. Once a year
   C. Never
   D. Once a month

32. What is a tippy tap? (1 mark)
   A. A cooking pot
   B. A type of soap
   C. A toothbrush
   D. A simple hand-washing device made from a container

33. Should you share a toothbrush? (1 mark)
   A. Yes with friends
   B. Only at school
   C. Yes with family
   D. No

34. Why should stagnant water be emptied from tins and tyres? (1 mark)
   A. It smells of soap
   B. It is too clean
   C. Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   D. It cools the compound

35. Which waste should not be burnt because the smoke is harmful? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic
   B. Dry leaves
   C. Wood
   D. Paper

36. Why stuff canvas shoes with paper after washing? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them wet
   B. It makes them heavier
   C. It makes them dirty
   D. It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture

37. Why should chemicals not be used to clean PPE unless an adult directs you? (1 mark)
   A. They can harm the skin and the material
   B. They cool the PPE
   C. They are too cheap
   D. They make it too clean

38. How should rubber gloves be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a fire
   B. Leave them dirty
   C. Wash with a stone
   D. Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry

39. How should you carry scissors? (1 mark)
   A. Running
   B. With the points held down
   C. By the blades
   D. With the points up

40. When is even tacking most useful? (1 mark)
   A. Only for paper
   B. Only for straight seams that need no hold
   C. When you do not want to sew
   D. For curves and slippery cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to boil potatoes. (4 marks)

42. Explain how good personal hygiene helps prevent diseases such as diarrhoea. (4 marks)

43. Describe how to clean gumboots. (4 marks)

44. List four basic needs of domestic animals. (4 marks)

45. Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly? (2 marks)

46. Describe how to wash hands correctly. (4 marks)

47. Explain what is meant by direct sowing. (2 marks)

48. Give three uses of goats. (3 marks)

49. Name the three main food groups and one example of each. (3 marks)

50. Give two reasons why goats are suitable for dry areas. (2 marks)

51. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

52. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

53. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

54. Why should gumboots not be dried near a hot fire? (2 marks)

55. Why must a passion fruit plant have a trellis? (2 marks)

56. How can you tell that compost is ready for use? (3 marks)

57. Name two other ways of saving water in the garden. (2 marks)

58. Explain the steps for dusting a room. (4 marks)

59. Describe how to make long and short tacking. (4 marks)

60. Why should vegetables not be boiled for a long time? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The disease can spread to the crops later
   Disease germs may survive and infect crops when the compost is used.

2. A — It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   It turns waste into useful manure.

3. C — It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   Soil and old compost carry bacteria and fungi that break down wastes.

4. D — It attracts rats and flies and smells bad
   Meat and fatty food attract pests and create a bad smell.

5. D — It is dark, crumbly and smells like fresh earth
   Ready compost looks and smells like soil and the materials cannot be recognised.

6. A — Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   A covering of dry grass slows down drying of the soil.

7. A — The holes may block
   Dirt gets stuck in tiny holes.

8. C — So water does not run out of the end
   An open end would waste water.

9. D — By burning wood slowly with little air
   Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

10. D — A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

11. B — Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   The seedlings are never moved.

12. C — Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   Sowing is planting seeds.

13. A — They take water, light and food from the crop
   Weeds compete with crops.

14. A — Extra water can drain out
   Waterlogged soil rots seeds and roots.

15. D — Carry water and food between roots and leaves
   The trunk is like a pipe for the plant.

16. C — A woody fruit tree that grows in cooler highlands
   Tree tomato is a woody tree fruit.

17. A — When they are ripe
   Ripe fruit is tastiest and has the most vitamins.

18. D — Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   Peaceful protection.

19. D — Mango tree
   Big trees like mango take several years.

20. A — To remove air spaces and hold the roots
   Air pockets dry out roots.

21. D — Mutton
   Mutton is sheep meat.

22. A — Beef
   Beef comes from cattle.

23. D — Chick
   A chick is a young chicken.

24. A — Protein
   Protein builds muscles.

25. C — Pick one or more foods from each group
   A balanced meal includes all three groups.

26. B — Groundnuts
   Groundnuts give protein and energy.

27. D — Vegetables and fruits
   Fibre helps digestion.

28. B — Potatoes
   Potatoes are commonly boiled.

29. C — A dry cloth or oven gloves
   Wet cloth lets heat through.

30. C — About 10 minutes
   Ten minutes of gentle boiling makes hard eggs.

31. A — Twice a day
   Morning and before bed.

32. D — A simple hand-washing device made from a container
   A tippy tap uses little water.

33. D — No
   Toothbrushes carry germs.

34. C — Mosquitoes lay eggs in it
   Mosquitoes spread malaria.

35. A — Plastic
   Burning plastics gives harmful smoke.

36. D — It keeps their shape and soaks up moisture
   Paper absorbs water.

37. A — They can harm the skin and the material
   Chemicals can be dangerous.

38. D — Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

39. B — With the points held down
   This avoids injury.

40. D — For curves and slippery cloth
   Even tacking holds firmly.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wash, peel and cut into equal pieces; put in a pot with water and salt; cover and boil for about 15 to 20 minutes until soft; drain the water carefully.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Washing hands removes germs before they reach the mouth. Safe water and clean food stop germs entering the body. Using the toilet and washing hands afterwards stops germs from spreading.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean water, enough feed, clean shelter, health care and kind handling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each need.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with example.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: They eat leaves, shrubs and grass, and can live where cattle find little to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Heat can crack the rubber and spoil the boots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for heat, 1 mark for cracking.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Its stem is soft and cannot stand, so the trellis supports it as it climbs and spreads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soft stem, 1 mark for support.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open windows; use a slightly damp clean cloth; dust from high to low; shake and wash the duster outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Long boiling removes vitamins into the water, so they lose their goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.
